I gave Sonnet 5.5 one photo of a rescue truck. It came back with a 2,766-piece LEGO set and a 39-page manual.

It took a few follow-up prompts to get it perfect, but it moved through a project this size faster than I thought, and the quality held up from the first render to the last page of the manual.

The prompt I started with:
"I want to build a detailed LEGO set of this truck in the picture.

I want it to be feature complete, include motion and interactivity where possible, and be of the quality a LEGO master builder would be proud of.

I want the final output to include a rendering of the LEGO set, all of the pieces I need to order from LEGO, the instruction manual to build it, and a local website I can interact with to see it built piece by piece."

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

For everyone who insists on seeing AI as nothing but a tool. You only see what you let yourself see.

LOW RES

Made with Opus 5.5 & GPT-5.5

Today we are launching Muse for Small Business, a collection of connectors that allows businesses to run, grow, and create new opportunities.

Every great American boom is the same story: scarcity becomes abundance, and GDP takes off.

In 1865, moving goods across America was scarce. Then rail track grew from 35,000 miles to over 192,000 by 1900, freight volumes tripled in thirteen years, and a farmer in Kansas could suddenly sell to a buyer in Boston. 

Communication went from scarce to abundant with the telegraph, then the telephone, so a shopkeeper could check prices, place orders, and chase debts without leaving the counter. 

Steel went from precious to plentiful: by 1913, American mills out-produced all of Europe, which meant cheaper buildings, cheaper machines, and cheaper tools for every workshop in the country. 

Each scarcity that fell unlocked a wave of small enterprises, and AI is giving us another wave.

Building Muse for Small Business is a step toward how we make that abundance again: every business owner gets the tools and firepower that used to only belong to large companies. 

We've seen this movie before, and it always ends with more prosperity than the pessimists thought possible. 

The future is for everyone and today we're excited to accelerate that future http://muse.ai/business
